title.en: Early nationalist stirrings in Tamil Nadu

text.en: In 1877 T. Muthuswami became the first Indian judge of the Madras High Court, and the English-owned press howled against it. Angry educated young men decided Indians needed a newspaper of their own.

Tamil Nadu led the resistance: the Palayakarars fought in the late eighteenth century and the sepoys rose at Vellore Fort in 1806.
With Western education came an educated middle class, so the struggle later took a constitutional path.
The Madras Native Association of 1852, begun by Gazulu Lakshminarasu and Srinivasanar, was the earliest South Indian organisation for public interests.
It campaigned against the torture of peasants by revenue officials, leading to a Torture Commission and abolition of the Torture Act.
By 1862 the Madras Native Association had ceased to exist.
The appointment of T. Muthuswami as High Court judge in 1877 was criticised by the European-owned press.
In 1878 G. Subramaniam, M. Veeraraghavachari and four friends started The Hindu, and in 1891 Subramaniam began the Tamil Swadesamitran, a daily from 1899.
The Madras Mahajana Sabha was started on 16 May 1884 by Veeraraghavachari, Anandacharlu and Rangaiah, who became its first president.
Leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji, K.T. Telang and Surendranath Banerjee met at Adyar in December 1884 before the Congress was formed.
At the first Congress session in Bombay in 1885, 22 of the 72 delegates were from Madras.
The third session, at Madras in 1887, had Badruddin Tyabji as president, and 362 of 607 delegates came from the Madras Presidency.
These early nationalists, such as V.S. Srinivasanar, P.S. Sivasamy and G.A. Natesan, held hall meetings, worked in English and used constitutional methods, so they were later called moderates.

problem.en: Why was The Hindu started and who started it?

text.en: Europeans owned the press in 1877, and it attacked Muthuswami's appointment as judge.

why.en: Educated Indians felt they had no voice.

text.en: G. Subramaniam, M. Veeraraghavachari and four friends started The Hindu in 1878.

why.en: It became a vehicle of nationalist propaganda.

text.en: Subramaniam also began Swadesamitran in Tamil.
